messages:
maria: Quick follow-up on the 'unbundling' idea from last week's RFC — we need a short thread to converge on a path forward for service identity surfaces. Ops flagged two immediate problems with the current proposal: 1) Dedicated customers want minimal org-wide keys, and 2) our proxy stack still expects a long-lived token for telemetry.

sam: Can you sketch the concrete tradeoffs again? i remember the RFC suggested project-scoped API keys + exchange for ephemeral runtime creds.

maria: Exactly. The goal is: project-scoped long-lived keys for admin/CI flows; ephemeral, short-lived tokens for runtime service-to-service calls. Exchange would be done via a broker with strict audience/ttl checks.

andrew: Main engineering concern: broker adds latency and operational surface. Also how do we handle cross-project proxies that need to act on behalf of multiple projects?

lee: For cross-project proxies we either: (A) allow a proxy to hold multiple project-scoped tokens (bad ops UX), or (B) require the proxy to present an actor identity + request exchange per call (adds chattiness).

maria: Ops prefers (B) — they like short-lived actor proofs so a leaked proxy token is less blast radius. But we should quantify latency.

sam: Rough numbers — current internal exchange path is ~12ms p50 on our infra. With authz checks and KV lookup maybe ~25-30ms. That seems acceptable for non-top-latency RPCs but could be noisy for hot paths.

andrew: Suggestion: cache proofs at the proxy for TTL 1s with jitter to avoid stampedes. That gets most of the benefits while keeping exchange calls low.

lee: Also need to consider RBAC translation: project-scoped token might not carry all granular role claims. Do we have inline role assertions or do we require a separate call to authz service?

maria: Prefer embedding minimal claims in the ephemeral token: {"proj":"proj-123","actor":"svc-x","scope":"write:models"}. For anything beyond that, call authz. Keep token parsing cheap.

sam: Implementation nit: tokens should be compact (JWT-lite) and signed with our HSM-protected key. No heavy JSON blobs.

andrew: One more edge: third-party webhooks. They can't do token exchange easily. We need to define a passthrough pattern or an outbound signed webhook key with restricted scopes and TTL.

lee: Could expose a webhook issuance API that mints one-time short tokens (TTL 5m) scoped to a single endpoint and url-hash. That limits replay.

maria: Good. Action items: (1) andrew to prototype broker + TTL caching (2) sam to run a perf microbenchmark for 25ms vs 50ms vs 100ms latencies on hot RPCs (3) lee to write webhook issuance shape and a small schema for embedded claims.

andrew: I'll do a simple Go prototype by EOW, will include cache shim and metrics.

sam: I'll add a perf harness using our internal qps-sim and post numbers in this thread next week.

lee: I'll draft the webhook API and example request/response. Will include `POST /v1/webhooks/issue` example and suggested response:```json
{
  "token":"ey..",
  "expires_at":"2025-01-15T12:34:56Z",
  "scope":"webhook:ingest:proj-123"
}
```

maria: FYI we'll need a short RFC addendum for the gateway team documenting the proxy caching TTL and fallback heuristics (cache miss -> synchronous exchange). Please CC gateway-eng.

infra-bot: note: created ticket INFRA-1729 to track broker prototype. Assigned to andrew. :white_check_mark:

sam: @maria one policy question — do we allow org-admin keys to mint project-scoped tokens? or require a separate flow?

maria: Org-admins can mint, but issuance must be auditable and require MFA for UI flows. For CI flows we require a dedicated service account with a constrained key. We'll capture this in the RFC addendum.

andrew: Clarify failure modes: when exchange fails, proxy should fall back to an immutable read-only token if configured, else fail closed. Need explicit config per proxy route.

lee: +1 for explicit config. Also add a rate-limit on exchange per actor to avoid token storm during large rollouts.

maria: Great. I'll compile the notes and write the addendum draft. Putting a tentative deadline for the addendum + perf numbers: next Wednesday. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
